chosenStory: Luxury retailers reportedly considering bid for De Beers
whyThisStory: Luxury retailers buying a mining business offers the clearest insider joke: merchandising a pickaxe as this season’s must-have accessory.
setting: a luxury leather-goods boutique display alcove
sceneDescription: A luxury boutique has given a battered mining pickaxe the full handbag treatment, complete with a silk-wrapped handle, because apparently buying a mine starts with accessorising the equipment. In a pale limestone display alcove, one small, visibly used pickaxe rests diagonally on a cream suede presentation cushion. An immaculate burgundy silk scarf is wound around its wooden grip and finished in a neat bow, exactly like a handbag-handle scarf. The surrounding boutique is understated and empty; the incongruity is entirely between the rugged tool and its precious retail presentation.
finalImagePrompt: An unpeopled luxury leather-goods boutique with pale limestone walls and an ivory display plinth. A battered mining pickaxe rests diagonally on a cream suede presentation cushion; its wooden grip is meticulously wrapped in burgundy silk with a neat bow. This small display sits in the middle, lower half, occupying less than one-third of the image width. Plain wall above. Natural window light, genuine steel scratches, worn wood, slightly creased silk. No writing, logos or stones.
